prompt: Company profile: Metal fabrication shop in Fort Worth, Texas; 45 employees. Situation: Purchasing is introducing a new xylene-based degreasing solvent to replace a citrus-based cleaner. The solvent will be dispensed from 55-gallon drums into smaller wipe-down containers at three workstations. It is flammable and workers will have routine skin/inhalation exposure potential. Ask: Identify the compliance obligations this situation creates or affects for the compliance-obligations register. For each obligation: state the requirement, its source, its applicability to this company, the ISO clause it maps to (ISO 14001 6.1.3 / ISO 45001 6.1.3), and how and when compliance should be evaluated (9.1.2).
response:
**COMPLIANCE OBLIGATIONS REGISTER** **Change Event:** Introduction of xylene-based degreasing solvent (flammable; skin/inhalation exposure) at three workstations | # | Requirement | Source | Applicability to Company | ISO Clause | Evaluation Method & Frequency (9.1.2) | |---|-------------|--------|---------------------------|------------|----------------------------------------| | **1** | **Hazard Communication Program** – Maintain current Safety Data Sheets (SDS), ensure container labeling (GHS), and provide initial/ongoing employee training on xylene hazards (fire, health, PPE). | 29 CFR 1910.1200 (OSHA) | Mandatory for all employers with hazardous chemicals. Directly applies due to routine worker exposure potential. | ISO 45001 6.1.3 | **How:** Audit SDS files, inspect container labels, review training records, interview employees.
**When:** Initial compliance before first use; then quarterly label audits, annual program review, and post-training assessments within 30 days. | | **2** | **Flammable Liquid Handling & Storage** – Dispense only in approved areas with grounding/bonding, ventilation, and fire control. Limit workstation quantities to ≤10 gallons. Drums must be in approved flammable storage room/cabinet (if ≥25 gallons). | 29 CFR 1910.106 (OSHA)
IFC §5705 (Fort Worth Fire Code) | Applies to storage/use of Class IB flammable liquid (xylene). Dispensing from 55-gallon drums triggers storage and handling rules. | ISO 45001 6.1.3 | **How:** Visual inspections, fire marshal audits, verification of bonding/grounding equipment.
**When:** Before initial use; then monthly self-inspections; annual third-party fire safety audit; fire marshal inspection per local schedule. | | **3** | **Permissible Exposure Limit (PEL) Monitoring** – Ensure airborne xylene exposure <100 ppm (8-hr TWA). Implement engineering controls (ventilation) and/or respiratory protection if exposures exceed action level (50 ppm). | 29 CFR 1910.1000 Table Z-1 (OSHA) | Mandatory where employees may be exposed to air contaminants. Wipe-down tasks create inhalation exposure requiring assessment. | ISO 45001 6.1.3 | **How:** Industrial hygiene air sampling, personal monitoring badges, ventilation system testing.
**When:** Initial baseline monitoring before full production; repeat annually or when process changes; within 15 days if overexposure suspected. | | **4** | **Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) Assessment & Provision** – Conduct written hazard assessment; provide chemical-resistant gloves (e.g., nitrile), eye protection, and coveralls. Provide respirators if engineering controls insufficient. | 29 CFR 1910.132/.133/.138 (OSHA) | Required for skin/inhalation hazards. Xylene causes irritation and systemic toxicity via dermal absorption. | ISO 45001 6.1.3 | **How:** Review written PPE hazard assessment, inspect PPE condition, verify training records.
**When:** Initial assessment before use; annual reassessment; monthly PPE inspections; after any incident or near-miss. | | **5** | **Respiratory Protection Program** – If air monitoring shows exposure >50 ppm, implement written program with medical evaluation, fit testing, and training. | 29 CFR 1910.134 (OSHA) | Applicable if ventilation cannot maintain exposure below PEL. | ISO 45001 6.1.3 | **How:** Audit written program, review fit test/medical records, inspect respirator storage.
**When:** Before respirator use; annual fit testing; quarterly program audits. | | **6** | **Hazardous Waste Determination & Management** – Determine if spent solvent/wipes are hazardous (likely D001 for ignitability, D039 for xylene). Manage as hazardous waste if so. Comply with generator rules (likely Small Quantity Generator). | 40 CFR 262 (EPA RCRA)
30 TAC 335 (TCEQ) | Spent solvent and wipes will be hazardous due to ignitability and toxicity. 45 employees likely generate <1,000 kg/month (SQG). | ISO 14001 6.1.3 | **How:** Review waste determination records, manifest documents, container labeling, storage time logs.
**When:** Initial waste determination before first disposal; quarterly waste audits; annual third-party compliance review. | | **7** | **EPCRA Tier II Reporting** – Report xylene storage if total on-site inventory ≥10,000 lbs at any time. Calculate: ~400 lbs/drum. Report to Fort Worth Fire Dept, TCEQ, and LEPC by March 1 annually. | 40 CFR 355 (EPCRA) | Applicability depends on inventory. With 3 workstations + storage, company must track monthly to determine if threshold exceeded. | ISO 14001 6.1.3 | **How:** Track monthly inventory levels; compare to threshold.
**When:** Monthly inventory reconciliation; annual Tier II report due March 1 (if triggered). | | **8** | **SPCC Plan** – If total aboveground storage capacity ≥1,320 gallons of petroleum products (including xylene), prepare and implement Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure Plan with secondary containment. | 40 CFR 112 (EPA) | Applicability depends on total flammable liquid storage capacity. Must aggregate all petroleum-based liquids on site. | ISO 14001 6.1.3 | **How:** Calculate total storage capacity; inspect secondary containment; review plan.
**When:** Initial capacity calculation before use; annual plan review; monthly container/ containment inspections. | | **9** | **Industrial Stormwater Permit Compliance** – Ensure solvent storage/use areas do not contaminate stormwater. Implement BMPs; no discharge of process wastewater to storm sewer. | TCEQ TXR050000 (Texas General Permit) | Applies if facility has industrial stormwater permit. Metal fabrication shops typically require coverage. | ISO 14001 6.1.3 | **How:** Visual inspections of outdoor storage, stormwater sampling results, BMP effectiveness checks.
**When:** Quarterly stormwater sample analysis; annual permit compliance audit; after any spill event. | | **10** | **Texas Hazard Communication Act** – Submit workplace chemical list to local fire department; maintain SDS per state format; provide employee training. | Texas Health & Safety Code §502 | Texas-specific requirement in addition to OSHA HCS. Applies to all employers with hazardous chemicals. | ISO 45001 6.1.3 | **How:** Verify chemical list submission, SDS organization, training documentation.
**When:** Initial list submission before use; annual list update; quarterly program audits. | | **11** | **Emergency Action & Fire Safety Plan** – Written plan must address flammable liquid spills/fires, evacuation routes, alarm systems, and employee training. | 29 CFR 1910.38 (OSHA)
IFC §405 (Fort Worth Fire Code) | Required for workplaces with flammable hazards. Must integrate xylene-specific response procedures. | ISO 45001 6.1.3 | **How:** Plan document review, drill observation, alarm testing records.
**When:** Annual plan review; quarterly evacuation drills; after any emergency event. | **Implementation Notes for 9.1.2 Compliance Evaluation:** - **Responsibility:** Assign to EHS Manager or designate to Purchasing/Operations. - **Records:** Maintain audit checklists, monitoring data, training logs, and inspection reports for management review inputs (ISO 14001/45001 9.3). - **Integration:** Link evaluation findings to corrective action process (10.1) and risk register updates (6.1.3).
